limitations: R-A canonical answers are fixed classification descriptions/class names; not item-specific hidden bridge or context-bound entity names.
Source-family/candidate-pair collapse is a conservative grouping proxy; aliases and common source templates can reduce independence further.
Arrays verified via headers, lengths and stored provenance only; no finite-value or numerical state validation performed.

No complete-name holdout is supplied by existing R-A splits: every substantive test target occurs in pool. New identity splits would need separate frozen construction and cannot turn fixed descriptions into hidden workspace names.
